#### What is Agency?

Our description of the physical stuff of the world, in the language of modern physics, paints a picture of Nature driven by extremum principles.
Energy minimization and entropy maximization guide this soup of particles, the *physical substrate*, towards thermodynamic equilibrium where, once there, nothing interesting ever happens.
Yet, in this inexorable slide towards inevitable boredom, matter organizes itself from atoms to crystals and catalytic networks, patterns forming and growing in complexity and scale.
And, if the conditions are just right, macroscopic structure supervenes over microscopic details giving birth to agency within the substrate.
Matter, once subject solely to the whims of energy and entropy, gains the ability to scream **No! Not today Equilibrium!**, to act to suppress its slide towards that inevitable end.
Our description of the physical stuff of the world, in the language of modern physics, does not know how matter does that.

As AI gets more sophisticated, the ethical question of whether it is alive will grow in importance over the coming decades.
My research is a cross-disciplinary approach towards trying to understand how agency emerges from the physical substrate of the world, a question of profound importance to humanity's understanding of itself, artificial intelligence, the biosphere both are a part of.
Living systems act teleologically; since prediction is the providence of information theory, my approach towards tackling this enormous question draws not just from the physical and life sciences, but computer science and machine learning, neuroscience, the philosophy of language, and epistemology.
A large component of this program is using the techniques of information theory to create informational narratives of systems complementing their traditional physical descriptions.
This means characterizing how information is generated, stored, and flows in biological, ecological, and sociological systems, and identifying relationships between subsystems that lead to these informational structures.

## About

### A Nerd and his three housemates

I am an affiliate of the [S.E.T.I. Institute](https://www.seti.org/), and a visiting researcher at the [University of Rochester's Department of Physics and Astronomy](https://www.pas.rochester.edu/).
I was born in Poland, grew up in Berlin and California.
I earned my B.A. in physics at the [University of California, Berkeley](https://physics.berkeley.edu/), and my theoretical physics Ph.D. in the lovely woods of New England from [Dartmouth College](https://physics.dartmouth.edu/).
At Cal I worked on neutrino detection for the [KamLAND project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamioka_Liquid_Scintillator_Antineutrino_Detector).
After undergrad I taught in N.Y.C. and researched low mass kinda-stars known as [brown dwarfs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_dwarf) at the reknowned [Hayden Planetarium](https://www.amnh.org/research/hayden-planetarium) located in the [American Museum of Natural History](https://www.amnh.org/).
For my Ph.D. I started off in [Cosmology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambda-CDM_model#:~:text=Inflation%20is%20a%20simple%20model,also%20determined%20by%20matching%20observations.), attending the prestigeous [Les Houches School of Physics](https://www.houches-school-physics.com/) summer program in the French Alps.
I slowly found my thoughts shifting from the very large to the subjective, about the nature of knowledge and how mushy brains come to know things about the world.
What exactly is information, how is it instantiated in the physical world, and how does it have causal power?
My thesis was on the behavior of information theoretic measures to the formation of [solitons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soliton) and [phase transitions.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critical_phenomena)

Since completing my doctorate I've been a research scientist in multiple fields: neuroscience, psychophysics, and continuum mechanics/biomedical physics.
During my time at the [Wisconsin Center for Sleep and Consciousness](https://centerforsleepandconsciousness.psychiatry.wisc.edu/people/) I worked on [Integrated Information Theory](https://www.iit.wiki/home), one of the leading theories of how subjective experience emerges in matter.
At the [Dartmouth-Hitchcock Medical Center](https://cim.dartmouth.edu/) I worked on a novel imaging modality known as [magentic resonance elastography](https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/magnetic-resonance-elastography/about/pac-20385177).
I was a fellow at the [Institute for Cross-Disciplinary Engagement](https://www.ice.dartmouth.edu/), giving me a multi-faceted perspective on the scientific endeavor.
At the University of Rochester I developed the viability based approach to semantic information theory, applying it to complex systems ranging from the [Kuramoto model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuramoto_model) of firefly synchronization to an exoplanet variant of Lovelock's famous Daisyworld.
None of these adventures would have been possible without the awesome power of mathematics coupled to creativity!

I have loved art and mathematics for as long as I can remember.
I'm keen on synthesizing the two, and make visualizations of the projects I work on.
After all, if a picture is worth a thousand words, then a thousand frames of video is, what, a million words?
That's also why I like mathematics.
It's a formal language that lets us convey the pictures in our heads with high fidelity to other people's heads.
And that is rad.

When not frantically scribbling runic looking symbols on paper, I like to go hiking with my GSD, Ursus.
He was born on 2023, still gives off major puppy vibes and so much energy.
At home I'm always greeted by my old man, Cosmas.
Cosmas was born in 2017, and is starting to get grey hairs and lose his teeth.
He likes lounging at home all day with his younger brother, Gaius, whose favorite past time is running up to Ursus, slapping him, and then running for dear life.
Animals are amazing, and I'm grateful to have these three guys in my life.

### Research

#### What is Information?

Information is a slippery concept.
Is it a subjective quantity or an objective one?
It's probably clear that there's information in a book.
What about a book written in a language you don't understand?
The book may be informative to someone, even if it is not informative to you, so it still contains information.
What if the book is written in a language that no living person can read?
Does it still contain information?
To describe these situations more precisely one needs to distill information that has meaning from the information that doesn't.
Subjective, meaningful information is *semantic*.
The structural aspects of information, which may or may not have semantics, is referred to as *syntactic*.

Surprisingly (pun intended, IYKYK), syntactic information is closely related to entropy, an objective aspect of the physical world.
Take the microcanonical definition of entropy as the number of microstates in a given macrostate; for example imagine all the ways that the stuff in your bedroom could be positioned.
A cheeky way of describing entropy is to say that there are WAAAY more ways for your bedroom to be disorganized than there are ways of it being organized.
Where is your favorite shirt?
In a disorganized room, you may have to look in many places before you find it, the room is said to have higher entropy.
Entropy is synonymous with uncertainty - the more uncertain you are about the exact state of your bedroom, the more entropy it has.
When you look around your bedroom you discount areas where the shirt is not, becoming more certain about where the shirt actually is.
The information you gain reduces your uncertainty; the entropy of the room is smaller the more you know about it!

Wait up. Hold on. Didn't that last paragraph start by saying entropy is an *objective* aspect of the world?
Why are we talking about *subjective* uncertainty?
Thermodynamic entropy is related to the temperature of a system.
How can looking around for a particular molecule (your favorite one) in a gas, change the temperature of the gas?!
The subjective and the objective shake hands to create what seems like a paradox.
When you find your favorite shirt in your messy room, you grab it and put it on.
Or put it into a dresser drawer.
Whatever.
The point is that you organize your room a little with the information you gain.
Similarly, one can use the information about a particular molecule in a gas to change the temperature of the gas.
James Clerk Maxwell first described such a *neat fingered being* in 1867, and dubbed *Maxwell's Demon* several years later by Lord Kelvin.
The demon sits at a tiny doorway between two volumes of gas at equal temperature.
When it sees a fast moving molecule approaching the door from the right, it lets it through.
Similarly, if it sees a slow moving molecule moving from the left it also lets it through.
By observing the gas, and acting on that information, the demon can make the gas on the left get hotter, while the gas on the right cools.
Why don't you try it:

- Maxwell's Demon (interactive applet)

Were you hired?

#### How does Agency emerge from Complexity?

Look at that.
It's like a little beastie, clamoring about in search of food.
It notices the directions in which its food supply is increasing, and turns towards them.
Sometimes it gets stuck between choices, shakes a little before choosing a particular option to move in.
It looks like its making choices, like its looking for food.
It's behavior looks complex, much like the behavior of paramecia under the microscope.
But is it?

What you're seeing is the simulation of a chemoton - a protocell consisting of a small collection of chemical species trapped inside a membrane.
The environment contains sources of another chemical species, one that is metabolized by the species in the membrane to produce more membrane.
As time goes by the membrane decays, causing the chemoton to shrink.
The motion you're seeing is due to the front end of the chemoton's membrane growing, and its back shrinking.

Seemingly complex behavior is what our eyes are drawn to, and agency is how our brains rationalize what they see.
That is not what is actually there.
This simple example of an incredibly basic system displaying complex, agent-like behavior is why finding agency is difficult.
We can't rely on a system behaving in a complicated way to justify the claim that the system is an agent.
For that matter, what exactly do we mean when we say *Agency*?
We are agents, right?
Entities capable of acting teleologically, of having goals and directing our actions towards attaining them.
By that definition, however, LLMs too are agents.
Whether one agrees or disagrees with that statement, it is clear that agency itself is still a nebulous concet.

Sweeping such concerns under the rug for the moment, when does a system transition from being purely mechanistic to having true agency?
The chemoton may not have agency, but does the paramecium?
Or is it, too, simply a bag of chemicals, reacting and metabolizing its surroundings, all the while fooling us into rationalizing it is something more?
I'm interested in models that live at this awkward boundary between automoton and agent.
Understanding how complexity, computation, and control intertwine to create behavioral autonomy will get us one very large step closer to understanding its emergence in the physical substrate.

AI poses the same problem to us as biology emerging from chemistry.
The current generation of LLMs have already passed the Turing test.
That type of complex, life-like behavior parallels the complex, life-like motions of the chemoton.

#### How do Complex Systems Evolve?

Life does not emerge from the soup of particles that is our Universe fully formed.
[Assembly theory](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06600-9) provides an excellent argument for why evolution starts as soon as molecules reach sizes of around 20 atoms:
the combinatorial explosion in possible molecular configurations vastly exceeds the exploratory ability of all the atoms in the universe!
Natural selection places pressure on any configurations that reach that size, leading to lineages of ever growing complexity.
What this implies is that evolution

## My Favorite Spacetimes

URL: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/

### The A- and B-Metrics of Ehlers and Kundt

The static vacuum fields of algebraic type D beside Schwarzschild's, which Tullio Levi-Civita constructed and Jürgen Ehlers and Wolfgang Kundt named in 1962: the A-metrics have a hyperbolic or a flat plane where Schwarzschild's field has a sphere, and the B-metrics exchange the time with an angle. Two of them, A II and B I, are the field of a tachyon, Schwarzschild's mass boosted past the speed of light, with a cone of unbounded curvature between them.

- id: `ab_metrics`
- tags: vacuum, static, stationary, Petrov type D, tachyon, Cherenkov cone, shock wave, hyperbolic symmetry, plane symmetric, Killing horizon, horizon, curvature singularity, Kruskal extension, maximal extension, wormhole, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/ab_metrics.json
- chart A II, Static: coordinates $(t, r, \chi, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(\dfrac{b}{r} - 1\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{\dfrac{b}{r} - 1} + r^2\left(d\chi^2 + \sinh^2\chi\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart A II, Inside the Cone: coordinates $(\sigma, z, \chi, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{d\sigma^2}{1 - \dfrac{b}{\sigma}} + \left(1 - \dfrac{b}{\sigma}\right)dz^2 + \sigma^2\left(d\chi^2 + \sinh^2\chi\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart A II, Kruskal: coordinates $(U, V, \chi, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{4b^3}{r}e^{-r/b}\,dU\,dV + r^2\left(d\chi^2 + \sinh^2\chi\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart A II, Inertial: coordinates $(T, X, Y, Z)$, $$ds^2 = -dT^2 + dX^2 + dY^2 + dZ^2 - \dfrac{b}{\sigma}\left(dZ^2 + \dfrac{\left(T\,dT - X\,dX - Y\,dY\right)^2}{\sigma\left(\sigma - b\right)}\right)$$
- chart B I, Static: coordinates $(\tau, r, \theta, z)$, $$ds^2 = r^2\left(-\sin^2\theta\,d\tau^2 + d\theta^2\right) + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{b}{r}} + \left(1 - \dfrac{b}{r}\right)dz^2$$
- chart B I, Outside the Cone: coordinates $(\tau, r, \phi, z)$, $$ds^2 = r^2\left(-d\tau^2 + \cosh^2\tau\,d\phi^2\right) + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{b}{r}} + \left(1 - \dfrac{b}{r}\right)dz^2$$
- chart B I, Through the Neck: coordinates $(\tau, \rho, \phi, z)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{b^2}{\left(1 - \rho^2\right)^2}\left(-d\tau^2 + \cosh^2\tau\,d\phi^2\right) + \dfrac{4b^2\,d\rho^2}{\left(1 - \rho^2\right)^4} + \rho^2dz^2$$
- chart B I, Inertial: coordinates $(T, X, Y, Z)$, $$ds^2 = -dT^2 + dX^2 + dY^2 + dZ^2 - \dfrac{b}{r}\left(dZ^2 - \dfrac{\left(T\,dT - X\,dX - Y\,dY\right)^2}{r\left(r - b\right)}\right)$$
- chart A III: coordinates $(t, r, \chi, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{b}{r}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{r}{b}dr^2 + r^2\left(d\chi^2 + \chi^2d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart B II, Static: coordinates $(\tau, r, \chi, z)$, $$ds^2 = r^2\left(-\sinh^2\chi\,d\tau^2 + d\chi^2\right) + \dfrac{dr^2}{\dfrac{b}{r} - 1} + \left(\dfrac{b}{r} - 1\right)dz^2$$
- chart B II, Through the Axis: coordinates $(\tau, \rho, \chi, z)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{b^2}{\left(1 + \rho^2\right)^2}\left(-\cosh^2\chi\,d\tau^2 + d\chi^2\right) + \dfrac{4b^2\,d\rho^2}{\left(1 + \rho^2\right)^4} + \rho^2dz^2$$
- chart B III: coordinates $(\tau, r, x, z)$, $$ds^2 = r^2\left(-d\tau^2 + dx^2\right) + \dfrac{r}{b}dr^2 + \dfrac{b}{r}dz^2$$

### Aichelburg-Sexl Ultraboost

The gravitational field of a massless particle, the Schwarzschild field boosted to the speed of light with its energy held fixed. Spacetime is flat on either side of a single null plane, which carries an impulsive gravitational shock wave with the particle at its centre.

- id: `aichelburg_sexl`
- tags: gravitational wave, shock wave, impulsive wave, pp-wave, massless particle, ultrarelativistic, boosted black hole, null source, vacuum, time-dependent, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model, Petrov type N
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/aichelburg_sexl.json
- chart Cartesian: coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 - \dfrac{4GE}{c^4}\ln\left(\dfrac{x^2 + y^2}{\rho_0^2}\right)\delta(ct - z)\left(c\,dt - dz\right)^2$$
- chart Null Cartesian: coordinates $(u, v, x, y)$, $$ds^2 = -du\,dv + dx^2 + dy^2 - \dfrac{4GE}{c^4}\ln\left(\dfrac{x^2 + y^2}{\rho_0^2}\right)\delta(u)\,du^2$$
- chart Null Cylindrical: coordinates $(u, v, \rho, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -du\,dv + d\rho^2 + \rho^2d\phi^2 - \dfrac{8GE}{c^4}\ln\left(\dfrac{\rho}{\rho_0}\right)\delta(u)\,du^2$$

### Alcubierre Warp Drive

A warp bubble metric that contracts space ahead of a ship and expands it behind, allowing travel that is effectively faster than light without locally exceeding light speed. It requires negative energy density (exotic matter) to sustain the bubble.

- id: `alcubierre`
- tags: warp drive, faster-than-light, exotic matter, negative energy, energy condition violation, time-dependent, idealized model, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/alcubierre.json
- chart Cartesian: coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + \left(dx - v_s f\,c\,dt\right)^2 + dy^2 + dz^2$$

### Anti-de Sitter

The maximally symmetric vacuum solution with constant negative curvature, arising from a negative cosmological constant. Its conformal boundary underpins the AdS/CFT correspondence in theoretical physics.

- id: `anti_de_sitter`
- tags: maximally symmetric, constant curvature, negative cosmological constant, cosmological constant, anti-de Sitter, AdS/CFT, holography, exact solution, static, homogeneous, isotropic, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model, Einstein space, conformally flat, stationary, spherically symmetric
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/anti_de_sitter.json
- chart Static global: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 + \dfrac{r^2}{L^2}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 + \dfrac{r^2}{L^2}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Poincare patch: coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{L^2}{z^2}\left(-c^2dt^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2\right)$$

### Anti-de Sitter Soliton

A smooth spacetime of negative energy with no horizon: the planar black hole of anti-de Sitter space with its time and one flat direction exchanged, so that the horizon becomes a tip where a circle shrinks to a point. Gary Horowitz and Robert Myers found it in 1998 and conjectured that it is the ground state of its boundary conditions.

- id: `ads_soliton`
- tags: static, stationary, soliton, no horizon, regular, negative energy, positive energy, ground state, Casimir energy, confinement, cosmological constant, negative cosmological constant, anti-de Sitter, AdS/CFT, holography, compact dimension, three-dimensional, four-dimensional, five-dimensional, higher dimensions, string theory, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, idealized model, Einstein space
- signature: (-,+,\ldots,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/ads_soliton.json
- chart Horowitz-Myers: coordinates $(t, r, \tau, x)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{r^2}{L^2}\left(-c^2dt^2 + \left(1 - \dfrac{r_0^3}{r^3}\right)d\tau^2 + dx^2\right) + \dfrac{L^2}{r^2}\dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_0^3}{r^3}}$$
- chart Poincaré: coordinates $(t, z, \tau, x)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{L^2}{z^2}\left(-c^2dt^2 + \left(1 - \dfrac{z^3}{z_0^3}\right)d\tau^2 + dx^2 + \dfrac{dz^2}{1 - \dfrac{z^3}{z_0^3}}\right)$$
- chart Polar: coordinates $(t, \rho, \phi, x)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{r_0^2}{L^2}\cosh^{4/3}(\tfrac{3\rho}{2L})\left(-c^2dt^2 + dx^2\right) + d\rho^2 + \dfrac{4L^2\sinh^2(\tfrac{3\rho}{2L})}{9\cosh^{2/3}(\tfrac{3\rho}{2L})}d\phi^2$$
- chart Five Dimensions: coordinates $(t, r, \tau, x, y)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{r^2}{L^2}\left(-c^2dt^2 + \left(1 - \dfrac{r_0^4}{r^4}\right)d\tau^2 + dx^2 + dy^2\right) + \dfrac{L^2}{r^2}\dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_0^4}{r^4}}$$
- chart Three Dimensions: coordinates $(t, r, \tau)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{r^2}{L^2}\left(-c^2dt^2 + \left(1 - \dfrac{r_0^2}{r^2}\right)d\tau^2\right) + \dfrac{L^2}{r^2}\dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_0^2}{r^2}}$$

### Black Hole Threaded by a Cosmic String

A Schwarzschild black hole with a straight cosmic string through it. Off the axis it is Schwarzschild's vacuum, and around the whole axis, horizon included, a wedge is missing whose angle the string's tension sets, which lowers the horizon's area and the black hole's energy at a fixed mass.

- id: `string_black_hole`
- tags: topological defect, cosmic string, conical, angular deficit, conical singularity, black hole, black hole hair, black hole thermodynamics, vacuum, static, stationary, axisymmetric, mass, curvature singularity, coordinate singularity, horizon, event horizon, causal structure, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/string_black_hole.json
- chart Static: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + b^2\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Static with the Wedge Removed: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \tilde\phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\tilde\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(u, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)du^2 - 2\,du\,dr + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + b^2\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)dv^2 + 2\,dv\,dr + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + b^2\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli Black Hole

A rotating black hole in three spacetime dimensions with a negative cosmological constant. It has constant negative curvature everywhere, being anti-de Sitter space with points identified by a discrete boost, and it carries a temperature and an entropy that can be computed exactly.

- id: `btz`
- tags: negative cosmological constant, cosmological constant, anti-de Sitter, constant curvature, black hole, BTZ black hole, rotating, rotating black hole, mass, angular momentum, horizon, event horizon, Cauchy horizon, causal structure, stationary, circularly symmetric, black hole thermodynamics, Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, AdS/CFT, holography, three-dimensional, 2+1 dimensional gravity, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, idealized model, Einstein space, conformally flat
- signature: (-,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/btz.json
- chart Stationary: coordinates $(t, r, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(\dfrac{r^2}{\ell^2} - M + \dfrac{J^2}{4r^2}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{\dfrac{r^2}{\ell^2} - M + \dfrac{J^2}{4r^2}} + r^2\left(d\phi - \dfrac{J}{2r^2}c\,dt\right)^2$$
- chart Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(v, r, \tilde\phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(\dfrac{r^2}{\ell^2} - M + \dfrac{J^2}{4r^2}\right)dv^2 + 2\,dv\,dr + r^2\left(d\tilde\phi - \dfrac{J}{2r^2}dv\right)^2$$
- chart Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(u, r, \tilde\phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(\dfrac{r^2}{\ell^2} - M + \dfrac{J^2}{4r^2}\right)du^2 - 2\,du\,dr + r^2\left(d\tilde\phi - \dfrac{J}{2r^2}du\right)^2$$

### Bardeen Regular Black Hole

A black hole with horizons and no singularity, which James Bardeen proposed in 1968. A ball of de Sitter space sits where Schwarzschild's singularity would be, and Eloy Ayón-Beato and Alberto García showed in 2000 that the field of a magnetic monopole in a nonlinear electrodynamics is its source.

- id: `bardeen`
- tags: regular black hole, black hole, static, stationary, spherically symmetric, mass, magnetic monopole, magnetic charge, nonlinear electrodynamics, de Sitter core, regular centre, singularity theorems, strong energy condition, weak energy condition, energy conditions, horizon, event horizon, Cauchy horizon, inner horizon, extremal black hole, mass inflation, causal structure, maximal extension, asymptotically flat, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/bardeen.json
- chart Static Spherical: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s\,r^2}{\left(r^2 + g^2\right)^{3/2}}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_s\,r^2}{\left(r^2 + g^2\right)^{3/2}}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(u, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s\,r^2}{\left(r^2 + g^2\right)^{3/2}}\right)du^2 - 2\,du\,dr + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s\,r^2}{\left(r^2 + g^2\right)^{3/2}}\right)dv^2 + 2\,dv\,dr + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Bartnik-McKinnon Soliton

A static ball of SU(2) Yang-Mills field held together by its own gravity, with a regular centre, no horizon, and flat space far away. Neither a Yang-Mills field nor gravity makes such a ball alone. No formula is known for it: the solutions are found by numerical integration, one for each number of zeros of the field, and every one of them is unstable.

- id: `bartnik_mckinnon`
- tags: soliton, particle-like solution, Yang-Mills field, Einstein-Yang-Mills, gauge field, numerical solution, sphaleron, regular centre, no horizon, asymptotically flat, instability, critical collapse, anisotropic, mass, static, stationary, spherically symmetric, isotropic coordinates, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/bartnik_mckinnon.json
- chart Areal Radius: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\sigma^2\left(1 - \dfrac{2m}{r}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{2m}{r}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Isotropic: coordinates $(t, \rho, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -f\,c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{h}{f}\left(d\rho^2 + \rho^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Tortoise: coordinates $(t, \xi, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = F\left(-c^2dt^2 + d\xi^2\right) + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Breitenlohner-Forgács-Maison: coordinates $(t, \tau, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -A^2N^2c^2dt^2 + r^2\left(d\tau^2 + d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Bell-Szekeres Colliding Electromagnetic Waves

Two plane electromagnetic shock waves colliding head on in flat space. Where both have passed the spacetime is locally the Bertotti-Robinson universe, and the waves focus each other onto a Killing-Cauchy horizon with the curvature finite everywhere.

- id: `bell_szekeres`
- tags: electrovacuum, electromagnetic field, Einstein-Maxwell, plane wave, electromagnetic wave, colliding plane waves, shock wave, conformally flat, Bertotti-Robinson, Killing-Cauchy horizon, Cauchy horizon, fold singularity, nonlinear, exact solution, time-dependent, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/bell_szekeres.json
- chart Double Null: coordinates $(u, v, x, y)$, $$ds^2 = -2\,du\,dv + \cos^2\left(au - bv\right)dx^2 + \cos^2\left(au + bv\right)dy^2$$
- chart Time and Space: coordinates $(\xi, \eta, x, y)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{-d\xi^2 + d\eta^2}{2ab} + \cos^2\eta\,dx^2 + \cos^2\xi\,dy^2$$
- chart Regular: coordinates $(T, Z, X, Y)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{-\left(1 + Z^2\right)dT^2 + 2TZ\,dT\,dZ + \left(1 - T^2\right)dZ^2}{2ab\left(1 - T^2 + Z^2\right)} + \dfrac{\left(1 - Y^2\right)dX^2 + 2XY\,dX\,dY + \left(1 - X^2\right)dY^2}{2ab\left(1 - X^2 - Y^2\right)}$$
- chart Global: coordinates $(\chi, \rho, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{1}{2ab}\left(-\cosh^2\rho\,d\chi^2 + d\rho^2 + d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Kruskal-Szekeres: coordinates $(U, V, \eta, x)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{4\,dU\,dV}{\left(1 + 2abUV\right)^2} + \dfrac{d\eta^2}{2ab} + \cos^2\eta\,dx^2$$
- chart Bertotti-Robinson: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{1}{2ab\,r^2}\left(-dt^2 + dr^2 + r^2d\theta^2 + r^2\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Bertotti-Robinson Electrovacuum

A conformally flat electrovacuum solution with uniform electromagnetic field, geometrically the product of two spaces of two dimensions each (AdS₂ × S²). It appears as the limit near the horizon of an extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole.

- id: `bertotti_robinson`
- tags: electrovacuum, electromagnetic field, charged, conformally flat, static, stationary, exact solution, near-horizon limit, extremal, spherically symmetric, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model, homogeneous, product spacetime
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/bertotti_robinson.json
- chart Static throat: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{r^2}{b^2}c^2 dt^2 + \dfrac{b^2}{r^2}dr^2 + b^2 d\Omega^2$$
- chart Poincaré: coordinates $(t, x, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{b^2}{x^2}\left(-c^2 dt^2 + dx^2\right) + b^2 d\Omega^2$$

### Bianchi Anisotropic Cosmologies

A family of spatially homogeneous but generally anisotropic cosmologies classified by the symmetry group of their spatial slices. They generalize FLRW models to study anisotropy in the early universe.

- id: `bianchi`
- tags: cosmology, spatially homogeneous, homogeneous, anisotropic, Bianchi classification, exact solution, time-dependent, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/bianchi.json
- chart Type I, Cartesian: coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + a_1^2 dx^2 + a_2^2 dy^2 + a_3^2 dz^2$$

### Black Saturn

A black ring turning in balance around a spherical black hole in five dimensions, the exact vacuum solution Henriette Elvang and Pau Figueras built in 2007 by the inverse scattering method. Rotation alone holds the two apart, each drags the other around, and one mass and angular momentum can be shared between them in a continuum of ways.

- id: `black_saturn`
- tags: vacuum, stationary, rotating, black hole, black ring, multiple black holes, axisymmetric, angular momentum, mass, frame dragging, ergoregion, horizon, event horizon, horizon topology, black hole uniqueness, conical singularity, asymptotically flat, higher dimensions, five-dimensional, soliton, inverse scattering, rod structure, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/black_saturn.json
- chart Weyl: coordinates $(t, \rho, z, \psi, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{2W - 2V}c^2dt^2 + L^2\left(e^{2V}\left(d\psi - \dfrac{\Omega}{L}c\,dt\right)^2 + \rho^2e^{-2W}d\phi^2 + e^{2\nu}\left(d\rho^2 + dz^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Polar: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \psi, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{2W - 2V}c^2dt^2 + L^2e^{2V}\left(d\psi - \dfrac{\Omega}{L}c\,dt\right)^2 + \dfrac{r^4\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}{L^2}e^{-2W}d\phi^2 + \dfrac{r^2e^{2\nu}}{L^2}\left(dr^2 + r^2d\theta^2\right)$$
- chart Ring Coordinates, the Ring Alone: coordinates $(t, x, y, \psi, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{1 + \lambda y}{1 + \lambda x}\left(c\,dt - C\,R\,\dfrac{1 + y}{1 + \lambda y}d\psi\right)^2 + \dfrac{R^2\left(1 + \lambda x\right)}{\left(x - y\right)^2}\left(-\dfrac{\left(1 - y^2\right)\left(1 + \nu y\right)}{1 + \lambda y}d\psi^2 - \dfrac{dy^2}{\left(1 - y^2\right)\left(1 + \nu y\right)} + \dfrac{dx^2}{\left(1 - x^2\right)\left(1 + \nu x\right)} + \dfrac{\left(1 - x^2\right)\left(1 + \nu x\right)}{1 + \lambda x}d\phi^2\right)$$

### Black String

Schwarzschild's black hole extended along one more direction of space, a static vacuum solution of gravity in five or more dimensions whose horizon is a cylinder. Ruth Gregory and Raymond Laflamme showed in 1993 that ripples along it longer than about seven horizon radii grow, and numerical evolutions of that instability end in a naked singularity.

- id: `black_string`
- tags: vacuum, static, stationary, black string, black brane, p-brane, Gregory-Laflamme instability, instability, Rayleigh-Plateau, black hole, horizon, event horizon, cylindrical horizon, curvature singularity, naked singularity, cosmic censorship, higher dimensions, five-dimensional, six-dimensional, Kaluza-Klein, compact dimension, string theory, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,\ldots,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/black_string.json
- chart Schwarzschild: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi, z)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right) + dz^2$$
- chart Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi, z)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)dv^2 + 2\,dv\,dr + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right) + dz^2$$
- chart Kerr-Schild: coordinates $(T, r, \theta, \phi, z)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)c^2dT^2 + \dfrac{2r_s}{r}c\,dT\,dr + \left(1 + \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)dr^2 + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right) + dz^2$$
- chart Schwarzschild, Six Dimensions: coordinates $(t, r, \psi, \theta, \phi, z)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_h^2}{r^2}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_h^2}{r^2}} + r^2\left(d\psi^2 + \sin^2\psi\,d\theta^2 + \sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right) + dz^2$$

### Bonnor Beam of Light

The exact gravitational field of a steady beam of light, which William Bonnor found in 1969, a plane-fronted gravitational wave that keeps pace with the light. A ray moving with the beam feels nothing, a ray moving against it is drawn in, and two beams shining the same way do not attract each other.

- id: `light_beam`
- tags: null dust, light beam, pp-wave, gravitational wave, Petrov type N, cylindrical symmetry, stationary, gravitational lensing, not asymptotically flat, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/light_beam.json
- chart Cartesian: coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 - A\left(c\,dt - dz\right)^2$$
- chart Null Cartesian: coordinates $(u, v, x, y)$, $$ds^2 = -2\,du\,dv + dx^2 + dy^2 - 2A\,du^2$$
- chart Null Cylindrical, Inside the Beam: coordinates $(u, v, \rho, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -2\,du\,dv + d\rho^2 + \rho^2d\phi^2 - \dfrac{8\pi G\epsilon}{c^4}\rho^2\,du^2$$
- chart Null Cylindrical, Outside the Beam: coordinates $(u, v, \rho, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -2\,du\,dv + d\rho^2 + \rho^2d\phi^2 - \dfrac{8\pi G\epsilon}{c^4}R^2\left(1 + 2\ln\left(\dfrac{\rho}{R}\right)\right)du^2$$

### Bonnor's Stars of Charged Dust

Stars of dust in which every grain carries just enough charge for its electric repulsion to cancel its gravity, so the dust rests in equilibrium with no pressure, in a ball or in any other shape. William Bonnor built a sphere of it in 1965, and in 1975 he and S. B. P. Wickramasuriya made one whose surface lies as close to its own horizon as one likes, so that light from its centre arrives with a redshift as large as one likes. José Lemos and Erick Weinberg named that limit a quasiblack hole.

- id: `bonnor_charged_dust`
- tags: dust, charged dust, charged, electric charge, electromagnetic field, Einstein-Maxwell, extremal, static, stationary, spherically symmetric, stellar interior, matched solution, regular centre, no horizon, black hole mimicker, quasiblack hole, gravitational redshift, quasar, harmonic coordinates, isotropic coordinates, mass, asymptotically flat, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/bonnor_charged_dust.json
- chart Harmonic: coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{c^2dt^2}{U^2} + U^2\left(dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2\right)$$
- chart Bonnor's Sphere of 1965: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{c^2dt^2}{U^2} + U^2\left(dr^2 + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Bonnor and Wickramasuriya's Sphere: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{c^2dt^2}{U^2} + U^2\left(dr^2 + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Isotropic Exterior: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 + \dfrac{m}{r}\right)^{-2}c^2dt^2 + \left(1 + \dfrac{m}{r}\right)^2\left(dr^2 + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Reissner-Nordström Exterior: coordinates $(t, R, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{m}{R}\right)^2c^2dt^2 + \left(1 - \dfrac{m}{R}\right)^{-2}dR^2 + R^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Spheroid Interior: coordinates $(t, u, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{c^2dt^2}{U^2} + U^2\left(a^2\left(\sinh^2u + \sin^2\theta\right)\left(du^2 + d\theta^2\right) + a^2\cosh^2u\cos^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Spheroid Exterior: coordinates $(t, u, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{c^2dt^2}{U^2} + U^2\left(a^2\left(\sinh^2u + \sin^2\theta\right)\left(du^2 + d\theta^2\right) + a^2\cosh^2u\cos^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Lemos and Weinberg's Cloud: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{c^2dt^2}{U^2} + U^2\left(dr^2 + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$

### Bonnor's Magnetic Dipole

The static field of a mass with a magnetic dipole moment, the solution of the Einstein-Maxwell equations William Bonnor found in 1966. Roberto Emparan showed in 2000 that its two poles are extremal black holes with opposite magnetic charges, held apart by a strut on the axis between them.

- id: `bonnor_magnetic_dipole`
- tags: electrovacuum, Einstein-Maxwell, electromagnetic field, magnetic field, magnetic dipole, static, stationary, axisymmetric, black hole, charged black hole, multiple black holes, extremal, degenerate horizon, horizon, event horizon, conical singularity, mass, quadrupole, asymptotically flat, Petrov type I, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/bonnor_magnetic_dipole.json
- chart Bonnor: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{P^2}{Y^2}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{P^2Y^2}{Q^3}\left(\dfrac{dr^2}{Z} + d\theta^2\right) + \dfrac{Y^2Z\sin^2\theta}{P^2}d\phi^2$$

### Bonnor's Rotating Dust Cloud

A stationary, axially symmetric cloud of dust in rigid rotation that thins out to nothing in every direction, found by William Bonnor in 1977. Its total mass is zero, its centre is a singularity of negative mass, and the circles about the axis inside a torus around the centre are closed timelike curves.

- id: `bonnor_rotating_dust`
- tags: dust, rotating, axisymmetric, stationary, closed timelike curves, asymptotically flat, angular momentum, frame dragging, negative mass, curvature singularity, naked singularity, directional singularity, Petrov type I, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/bonnor_rotating_dust.json
- chart Cylindrical: coordinates $(t, \rho, \phi, z)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(c\,dt - \dfrac{a^2\rho^2}{r^3}\,d\phi\right)^2 + \rho^2d\phi^2 + e^{a^4\rho^2(\rho^2 - 8z^2)/(8r^8)}\left(d\rho^2 + dz^2\right)$$
- chart Spherical: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(c\,dt - \dfrac{a^2\sin^2\theta}{r}\,d\phi\right)^2 + r^2\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2 + e^{a^4\sin^2\theta(9\sin^2\theta - 8)/(8r^4)}\left(dr^2 + r^2d\theta^2\right)$$

### Bonnor-Vaidya Charged Radiating Star

Vaidya's radiating star with a charge: the field of a spherical body that sends out, or takes in, null dust carrying electric charge as well as energy, found by William Bonnor and Prahlad Vaidya in 1970 as an exact solution of the Einstein-Maxwell equations. Its mass and its charge are functions of a null time, and where both are constant it is the charged black hole of Reissner and Nordström.

- id: `bonnor_vaidya`
- tags: null dust, charged null dust, charged, electric charge, electromagnetic field, Einstein-Maxwell, radiating, accreting, spherically symmetric, time-dependent, black hole, charged black hole, mass, horizon, event horizon, apparent horizon, Cauchy horizon, inner horizon, curvature singularity, naked singularity, weak energy condition, energy conditions, third law, self-similar, homothetic, Vaidya, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/bonnor_vaidya.json
- chart Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(u, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{2m}{r} + \dfrac{q^2}{r^2}\right)du^2 - 2\,du\,dr + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{2m}{r} + \dfrac{q^2}{r^2}\right)dv^2 + 2\,dv\,dr + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Homothetic: coordinates $(V, R, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = e^{2\mu V/M}\left(-\left(1 - \dfrac{2M}{R} + \dfrac{Q^2}{R^2} - \dfrac{2\mu R}{M}\right)dV^2 + 2\,dV\,dR + R^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$

### Born-Infeld Point Charge

The gravitational field of a point charge in Born and Infeld's electrodynamics, where the electric field stays finite at the charge, which Banesh Hoffmann found in 1935. With its whole mass in its field the charge is a particle with no horizon and a conical point at its centre, and with more mass it is a black hole with one horizon.

- id: `born_infeld_charge`
- tags: static, stationary, spherically symmetric, charged, electric charge, mass, point charge, electromagnetic mass, nonlinear electrodynamics, Born-Infeld electrodynamics, electromagnetic field, particle-like solution, geon, conical singularity, curvature singularity, naked singularity, timelike singularity, no horizon, black hole, charged black hole, horizon, event horizon, string theory, causal structure, maximal extension, asymptotically flat, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/born_infeld_charge.json
- chart Static Spherical: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{2m}{r}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{2m}{r}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(u, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{2m}{r}\right)du^2 - 2\,du\,dr + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{2m}{r}\right)dv^2 + 2\,dv\,dr + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Boson Stars and Geons

A ball of scalar field held together by its own gravity, the heir of John Wheeler's geon of light, found by David Kaup in 1968 and by Remo Ruffini and Silvano Bonazzola in 1969. The field turns in phase at a frequency $\omega$ while the spacetime stays static, with a regular centre and no horizon. The metric is known only numerically, as a solution of the Einstein-Klein-Gordon equations integrated outward from the centre, and the heaviest star has $M = 0.633\,M_P^2/m$ for bosons of mass $m$, with $M_P$ the Planck mass.

- id: `boson_star`
- tags: boson star, geon, scalar field, complex scalar field, minimally coupled scalar field, Einstein-Klein-Gordon, soliton, numerical solution, Kaup limit, maximum mass, no horizon, regular centre, black hole mimicker, exotic compact object, dark matter, Proca star, anisotropic pressure, isotropic coordinates, mass, asymptotically flat, static, stationary, spherically symmetric, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/boson_star.json
- chart Polar Areal: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\alpha^2c^2dt^2 + a^2dr^2 + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Isotropic: coordinates $(t, R, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\alpha^2c^2dt^2 + \psi^4\left(dR^2 + R^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$

### Boulware-Deser Black Hole

The spherical black hole of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity in five dimensions, which David Boulware and Stanley Deser found in 1985. The curvature squared term of string theory keeps its metric function finite at the centre and leaves a small mass with no horizon, and the same field equations have a second solution that approaches anti-de Sitter space.

- id: `boulware_deser`
- tags: static, stationary, spherically symmetric, hyperspherical symmetry, black hole, mass, Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, Gauss-Bonnet term, Lovelock gravity, higher curvature gravity, string theory, low energy string theory, higher dimensions, five-dimensional, curvature singularity, naked singularity, coordinate singularity, horizon, event horizon, white hole, maximal extension, causal structure, asymptotically flat, anti-de Sitter, ghost, instability, black hole thermodynamics, Hawking temperature, exact solution, Lorentzian, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/boulware_deser.json
- chart Hyperspherical: coordinates $(t, r, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 + \dfrac{r^2}{2\ell^2}\left(1 - \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{4\ell^2 r_0^2}{r^4}}\right)\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 + \dfrac{r^2}{2\ell^2}\left(1 - \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{4\ell^2 r_0^2}{r^4}}\right)} + r^2\left(d\psi^2 + \sin^2\psi\,d\theta^2 + \sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(u, r, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 + \dfrac{r^2}{2\ell^2}\left(1 - \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{4\ell^2 r_0^2}{r^4}}\right)\right)du^2 - 2\,du\,dr + r^2\left(d\psi^2 + \sin^2\psi\,d\theta^2 + \sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(v, r, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 + \dfrac{r^2}{2\ell^2}\left(1 - \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{4\ell^2 r_0^2}{r^4}}\right)\right)dv^2 + 2\,dv\,dr + r^2\left(d\psi^2 + \sin^2\psi\,d\theta^2 + \sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Hyperspherical, Anti-de Sitter Branch: coordinates $(t, r, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 + \dfrac{r^2}{2\ell^2}\left(1 + \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{4\ell^2 r_0^2}{r^4}}\right)\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 + \dfrac{r^2}{2\ell^2}\left(1 + \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{4\ell^2 r_0^2}{r^4}}\right)} + r^2\left(d\psi^2 + \sin^2\psi\,d\theta^2 + \sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Brill's Time-Symmetric Gravitational Waves

One moment of a spacetime that holds gravitational waves and nothing else, which Dieter Brill constructed in 1959. It is a single slice of space, three dimensions with no time, at the moment the wave is at rest, and it satisfies Einstein's constraint equations with no matter anywhere. Brill proved its mass positive, a strong enough wave already lies inside its own apparent horizon, and what the wave does afterwards is known from computer simulations.

- id: `brill_waves`
- tags: three-dimensional, Riemannian, no time, initial data, spatial slice, time symmetric, constraint equations, Hamiltonian constraint, gravitational wave, Brill wave, axisymmetric, conformal transformation, positive energy, positive mass theorem, mass, apparent horizon, minimal surface, trapped surface, critical collapse, gravitational collapse, geometrodynamics, geon, numerical relativity, numerical solution, asymptotically flat, Einstein equations, idealized model
- signature: (+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/brill_waves.json
- chart Brill: coordinates $(\rho, z, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = \psi^4\left(e^{2q}\left(d\rho^2 + dz^2\right) + \rho^2d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Spherical: coordinates $(r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = \psi^4\left(e^{2q}\left(dr^2 + r^2d\theta^2\right) + r^2\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Without Axial Symmetry: coordinates $(\rho, z, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = \psi^4\left(e^{2q}\left(d\rho^2 + dz^2\right) + \rho^2d\phi^2\right)$$

### C-Metric Accelerating Black Holes

An exact vacuum solution describing two black holes that accelerate away from each other, driven by a cosmic string or a strut along their axis of symmetry. With the acceleration set to zero it is the Schwarzschild black hole.

- id: `c_metric`
- tags: vacuum, static, axisymmetric, black hole, accelerating black hole, acceleration horizon, event horizon, horizon, Killing horizon, boost symmetry, cosmic string, conical singularity, Petrov type D, gravitational wave, curvature singularity, maximal extension, causal structure, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model, stationary
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/c_metric.json
- chart Spherical: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{1}{\left(1 + \alpha r\cos\theta\right)^2}\left(-\left(1 - \alpha^2r^2\right)\left(1 - \dfrac{2m}{r}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{\left(1 - \alpha^2r^2\right)\left(1 - \dfrac{2m}{r}\right)} + \dfrac{r^2d\theta^2}{1 + 2\alpha m\cos\theta} + C^2\left(1 + 2\alpha m\cos\theta\right)r^2\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Hong-Teo: coordinates $(\tau, y, x, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{1}{\alpha^2\left(x + y\right)^2}\left(\left(1 - y^2\right)\left(1 - 2\alpha m y\right)d\tau^2 - \dfrac{dy^2}{\left(1 - y^2\right)\left(1 - 2\alpha m y\right)} + \dfrac{dx^2}{\left(1 - x^2\right)\left(1 + 2\alpha m x\right)} + C^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\left(1 + 2\alpha m x\right)d\phi^2\right)$$

### Chandrasekhar-Xanthopoulos Colliding Plane Waves

Two plane gravitational waves colliding head on in flat space, each an impulse with a shock wave behind it, their polarizations out of line. Where both have passed the spacetime is locally Kerr's between its horizons, and the waves focus each other onto a Killing-Cauchy horizon with the curvature finite.

- id: `chandrasekhar_xanthopoulos`
- tags: vacuum, plane wave, gravitational wave, colliding plane waves, impulsive wave, shock wave, Kerr, Petrov type D, Killing-Cauchy horizon, Cauchy horizon, inner horizon, black hole interior, ring singularity, timelike singularity, fold singularity, nonlinear, exact solution, time-dependent, Lorentzian, four-dimensional, idealized model, Einstein equations
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/chandrasekhar_xanthopoulos.json
- chart Chandrasekhar-Xanthopoulos: coordinates $(\eta, \mu, x, y)$, $$ds^2 = m^2X\left(-\dfrac{d\eta^2}{1 - \eta^2} + \dfrac{d\mu^2}{1 - \mu^2}\right) + \dfrac{Y}{X}\left(dx - \dfrac{2q\left(\eta\left(1 - \mu^2\right) - p\left(\eta^2 - \mu^2\right)\right)}{Y}dy\right)^2 + \dfrac{\left(1 - \eta^2\right)\left(1 - \mu^2\right)X}{Y}dy^2$$
- chart Time and Space: coordinates $(\psi, \lambda, x, y)$, $$ds^2 = m^2X\left(-d\psi^2 + d\lambda^2\right) + \dfrac{Y}{X}\left(dx - \dfrac{2q\left(\sin\psi\cos^2\lambda - p\left(\sin^2\psi - \sin^2\lambda\right)\right)}{Y}dy\right)^2 + \dfrac{X\cos^2\psi\cos^2\lambda}{Y}dy^2$$
- chart Boyer-Lindquist: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{\Delta}{\Sigma}\left(dt - a\sin^2\theta\,d\phi\right)^2 + \dfrac{\Sigma}{\Delta}dr^2 + \Sigma\,d\theta^2 + \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\left(a\,dt - \left(r^2 + a^2\right)d\phi\right)^2$$
- chart Ingoing Kerr: coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \tilde\phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{\Delta}{\Sigma}\left(dv - a\sin^2\theta\,d\tilde\phi\right)^2 + 2\,dr\left(dv - a\sin^2\theta\,d\tilde\phi\right) + \Sigma\,d\theta^2 + \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\left(a\,dv - \left(r^2 + a^2\right)d\tilde\phi\right)^2$$

### Charged Shell of Dust

A thin spherical shell of charged dust, with flat spacetime inside it and Reissner-Nordström's field outside. Shrunk to a point at rest it is the classical point charge of Richard Arnowitt, Stanley Deser, and Charles Misner, with a finite mass set by its charge alone. Dropped from infinity with more charge than rest mass it falls through both horizons, turns round inside the inner one, and comes out into another universe.

- id: `charged_shell`
- tags: dust, thin shell, charged, electric charge, electromagnetic field, Einstein-Maxwell, gravitational collapse, bounce, matched solution, junction conditions, black hole, charged black hole, extremal, isotropic coordinates, point particle, mass, curvature singularity, timelike singularity, horizon, event horizon, Cauchy horizon, inner horizon, maximal extension, time-dependent, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat, causal structure, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/charged_shell.json
- chart Flat Interior: coordinates $(T, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2dT^2 + dr^2 + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Reissner-Nordström Exterior: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r} + \dfrac{r_q^2}{r^2}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r} + \dfrac{r_q^2}{r^2}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein Exterior: coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r} + \dfrac{r_q^2}{r^2}\right)dv^2 + 2\,dv\,dr + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein Exterior: coordinates $(u, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r} + \dfrac{r_q^2}{r^2}\right)du^2 - 2\,du\,dr + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Isotropic Exterior: coordinates $(t, \rho, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{\left(\rho^2 - ab\right)^2}{\left(\rho + a\right)^2\left(\rho + b\right)^2}c^2dt^2 + \left(1 + \dfrac{a}{\rho}\right)^2\left(1 + \dfrac{b}{\rho}\right)^2\left(d\rho^2 + \rho^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$

### Coleman-De Luccia Bubble

The spacetime of a false vacuum decaying, found by Sidney Coleman and Frank De Luccia in 1980. A bubble of lower vacuum energy appears by quantum tunnelling, its wall accelerates outward toward the speed of light, and the inside of the bubble is an open universe with no singularity at its start.

- id: `coleman_de_luccia`
- tags: vacuum decay, false vacuum, bubble, thin shell, matched solution, cosmology, open universe, hyperbolic space, inflation, de Sitter, anti-de Sitter, cosmological constant, spherically symmetric, time-dependent, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model, conformally flat
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/coleman_de_luccia.json
- chart Outside the Light Cone: coordinates $(\psi, \xi, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = d\xi^2 + \rho^2\left(-d\psi^2 + \cosh^2\psi\,d\theta^2 + \cosh^2\psi\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Open Universe: coordinates $(\tau, \chi, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2d\tau^2 + a^2\left(d\chi^2 + \sinh^2\chi\,d\theta^2 + \sinh^2\chi\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Open Universe, Conformal Time: coordinates $(\eta, \chi, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = a^2\left(-d\eta^2 + d\chi^2 + \sinh^2\chi\,d\theta^2 + \sinh^2\chi\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Static, Inside the Wall: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{\Lambda_T r^2}{3}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{\Lambda_T r^2}{3}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Static, Outside the Wall: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{\Lambda_F r^2}{3}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{\Lambda_F r^2}{3}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Curzon-Chazy Particle

A static, axially symmetric vacuum field whose Weyl potential is Newton's potential of a point mass, found by Jean Chazy in 1924 and H. E. J. Curzon in 1925. Its singularity is a naked ring of infinite circumference, and the curvature there depends on the direction of approach.

- id: `curzon_chazy`
- tags: vacuum, static, stationary, axisymmetric, Weyl class, harmonic function, mass, curvature singularity, naked singularity, directional singularity, ring singularity, asymptotically flat, Petrov type I, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/curzon_chazy.json
- chart Weyl: coordinates $(t, \rho, \phi, z)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{-2m/R}c^2dt^2 + e^{2m/R}\left(e^{-m^2\rho^2/R^4}\left(d\rho^2 + dz^2\right) + \rho^2d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Spherical: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{-2m/r}c^2dt^2 + e^{2m/r}\left(e^{-m^2\sin^2\theta/r^2}\left(dr^2 + r^2d\theta^2\right) + r^2\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Damour-Solodukhin Wormhole

Schwarzschild's metric with a small constant $\lambda^2$ added to $-g_{tt}$, which Thibault Damour and Sergey Solodukhin wrote down in 2007. The horizon becomes the throat of a static wormhole joining two asymptotically flat regions, and for small $\lambda$ an observer needs a time of order $(r_s/c)\ln(1/\lambda^2)$ to tell it from a black hole.

- id: `damour_solodukhin`
- tags: wormhole, traversable, black hole mimicker, black hole foil, exotic compact object, throat, no horizon, echoes, quasinormal modes, exotic matter, energy condition violation, static, stationary, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat, Einstein-Rosen bridge, Flamm's paraboloid, Lorentzian, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/damour_solodukhin.json
- chart Damour-Solodukhin: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r} + \lambda^2\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Rescaled Time: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{\left(1 + \lambda^2\right)r}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Through the Throat: coordinates $(t, \rho, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{\lambda^2\left(1 + \cosh\rho\right)}{2 + \lambda^2\left(1 + \cosh\rho\right)}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{r_s^2}{4\left(1 + \lambda^2\right)^2}\left(\lambda^2\left(1 + \cosh\rho\right)\left(2 + \lambda^2\left(1 + \cosh\rho\right)\right)d\rho^2 + \left(2 + \lambda^2\left(1 + \cosh\rho\right)\right)^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Isotropic: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(\left(\dfrac{4r - r_s}{4r + r_s}\right)^2 + \lambda^2\right)c^2dt^2 + \left(1 + \dfrac{r_s}{4r}\right)^4\left(dr^2 + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Einstein-Rosen: coordinates $(t, u, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(\dfrac{u^2}{u^2 + r_s} + \lambda^2\right)c^2dt^2 + 4\left(u^2 + r_s\right)du^2 + \left(u^2 + r_s\right)^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### de Sitter

The maximally symmetric vacuum solution with constant positive curvature, driven by a positive cosmological constant. It models an exponentially expanding empty universe and describes both inflation and the far future of our cosmos.

- id: `de_sitter`
- tags: maximally symmetric, constant curvature, positive cosmological constant, cosmological constant, de Sitter, inflation, expanding universe, cosmology, homogeneous, isotropic, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model, Einstein space, conformally flat, stationary, static, spherically symmetric
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/de_sitter.json
- chart Static Spherical: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{\Lambda r^2}{3}\right)c^2 dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{\Lambda r^2}{3}} + r^2 d\Omega^2$$
- chart Flat Slicing: coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + e^{2Ht}\left(dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2\right)$$

### Gibbons-Maeda-Garfinkle-Horowitz-Strominger Dilaton Black Hole

The static, spherically symmetric charged black hole of low energy string theory, a solution of Einstein's equations with a Maxwell field and a scalar field, the dilaton, coupled to it. On the plane of time and radius its metric is Schwarzschild's, with one horizon at the Schwarzschild radius for every charge and no inner horizon, and the area of its spheres vanishes at the singularity.

- id: `dilaton_black_hole`
- tags: static, stationary, spherically symmetric, charged, charged black hole, black hole, dilaton, scalar field, scalar hair, string theory, string metric, Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton, electric charge, magnetic charge, mass, electromagnetic field, extremal, supersymmetric, curvature singularity, coordinate singularity, horizon, event horizon, Hawking temperature, black hole shadow, causal structure, asymptotically flat, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/dilaton_black_hole.json
- chart Static Spherical: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}} + r\left(r - r_d\right)\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(u, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)du^2 - 2\,du\,dr + r\left(r - r_d\right)\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein: coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)dv^2 + 2\,dv\,dr + r\left(r - r_d\right)\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart String Metric, Magnetic Charge: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}}{1 - \dfrac{r_d}{r}}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)\left(1 - \dfrac{r_d}{r}\right)} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart String Metric, Electric Charge: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = \left(1 - \dfrac{r_d}{r}\right)\left(-\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}}\right) + \left(r - r_d\right)^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Double Kerr Solution

Two Kerr black holes on one axis of symmetry, the stationary vacuum solution Dietrich Kramer and Gernot Neugebauer built in 1980 by two Bäcklund transformations of flat space. The repulsion between the spins does not balance the attraction of the masses, so a strut on the axis between the horizons holds the holes apart.

- id: `double_kerr`
- tags: vacuum, stationary, axisymmetric, rotating, rotating black hole, black hole, multiple black holes, angular momentum, mass, conical singularity, ergosphere, frame dragging, horizon, event horizon, closed timelike curves, NUT parameter, soliton, superposition, black hole uniqueness, asymptotically flat, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/double_kerr.json
- chart Weyl-Lewis-Papapetrou: coordinates $(t, \rho, \phi, z)$, $$ds^2 = -f\left(c\,dt - \omega\,d\phi\right)^2 + \dfrac{1}{f}\left(e^{2\gamma}\left(d\rho^2 + dz^2\right) + \rho^2d\phi^2\right)$$

### Eguchi-Hanson Space

A space of four dimensions with no time in it, the gravitational instanton Tohru Eguchi and Andrew Hanson found in 1978: a solution of Einstein's vacuum equations with Riemannian signature and self dual curvature. Space closes on a 2-sphere of radius $a/2$, the bolt, and far away it is flat space with every point identified with its opposite.

- id: `eguchi_hanson`
- tags: vacuum, four-dimensional, gravitational instanton, Riemannian, Euclidean signature, no time, self-dual, hyperkähler, Kähler, asymptotically locally Euclidean, ALE space, bolt, nuts and bolts, lens space, orbifold, cotangent bundle, Gibbons-Hawking, multi-centre, Calabi, K3 surface, Hopf fibration, regular, exact solution, Einstein equations, idealized model
- signature: (+,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/eguchi_hanson.json
- chart Eguchi-Hanson: coordinates $(r, \theta, \phi, \psi)$, $$ds^2 = \left(1 - \dfrac{a^4}{r^4}\right)^{-1}dr^2 + \dfrac{r^2}{4}\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right) + \dfrac{r^2}{4}\left(1 - \dfrac{a^4}{r^4}\right)\left(d\psi + \cos\theta\,d\phi\right)^2$$
- chart Kähler Radius: coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi, \psi)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{\rho^2}{W}\left(d\rho^2 + \dfrac{\rho^2}{4}\left(d\psi + \cos\theta\,d\phi\right)^2\right) + \dfrac{W}{4}\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Gibbons-Hawking Two-Centre: coordinates $(\rho, z, \psi, \tau)$, $$ds^2 = V\left(d\rho^2 + dz^2 + \rho^2d\psi^2\right) + V^{-1}\left(d\tau + \omega\,d\psi\right)^2$$

### Einstein's Cluster

A static ball of particles on circular orbits in every direction, each held on its circle by the gravity of all the others, with no pressure along the radius. Einstein built it in 1939 to argue that no body can be squeezed inside its Schwarzschild radius, and it now serves as a model for halos of dark matter.

- id: `einstein_cluster`
- tags: Einstein cluster, star cluster, circular orbits, collisionless, anisotropic, tangential pressure, static, stationary, spherically symmetric, stellar interior, matched solution, mass, no horizon, dark matter, galactic halo, isotropic coordinates, three sphere, conical, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/einstein_cluster.json
- chart Areal Radius: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{2\Phi}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{2m}{r}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Constant Speed: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{1}{1 + 2V^2}\left(\dfrac{r}{R}\right)^{2V^2}c^2dt^2 + \left(1 + 2V^2\right)dr^2 + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Isotropic (Einstein): coordinates $(t, \rho, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -b\,c^2dt^2 + a\left(d\rho^2 + \rho^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Uniform Density (Florides): coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{R}\right)^{3/2}\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s r^2}{R^3}\right)^{-1/2}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_s r^2}{R^3}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Hyperspherical: coordinates $(t, \chi, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{\cos^3\chi_0}{\cos\chi}c^2dt^2 + a^2\left(d\chi^2 + \sin^2\chi\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$

### Einstein Static Universe

Albert Einstein's cosmology of 1917: dust spread uniformly through a round three sphere of fixed radius and held at rest by a positive cosmological constant. Minkowski, de Sitter, and anti-de Sitter space are each conformal to a region of it.

- id: `einstein_static`
- tags: cosmology, static, closed universe, three sphere, dust, cosmological constant, positive cosmological constant, Einstein cylinder, conformally flat, homogeneous, isotropic, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model, stationary, spherically symmetric
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/einstein_static.json
- chart Hyperspherical: coordinates $(t, \chi, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + R^2\left(d\chi^2 + \sin^2\chi\,d\theta^2 + \sin^2\chi\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Areal: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{R^2\,dr^2}{R^2 - r^2} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Einstein's Cartesian: coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 + \dfrac{\left(x\,dx + y\,dy + z\,dz\right)^2}{R^2 - x^2 - y^2 - z^2}$$

### Einstein-Rosen Bridge

The model of a particle that Albert Einstein and Nathan Rosen proposed in 1935: two identical sheets of space joined at a smallest sphere, the bridge. The neutral bridge is Schwarzschild's exterior taken twice and joined at $r = r_s$, and the charged bridge is Reissner and Nordström's metric with the sign of the electric term reversed, which needs no mass.

- id: `einstein_rosen_bridge`
- tags: wormhole, Einstein-Rosen bridge, throat, horizon, event horizon, Flamm's paraboloid, maximal extension, coordinate singularity, causal structure, static, stationary, spherically symmetric, mass, charged, electric charge, electromagnetic field, negative energy, energy condition violation, asymptotically flat, exact solution, Einstein equations, Lorentzian, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/einstein_rosen_bridge.json
- chart Einstein-Rosen: coordinates $(t, u, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{u^2}{u^2 + r_s}c^2dt^2 + 4\left(u^2 + r_s\right)du^2 + \left(u^2 + r_s\right)^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Schwarzschild: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Isotropic: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(\dfrac{4r - r_s}{4r + r_s}\right)^2c^2dt^2 + \left(1 + \dfrac{r_s}{4r}\right)^4\left(dr^2 + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Charged, Areal Radius: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r} - \dfrac{r_q^2}{r^2}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r_s}{r} - \dfrac{r_q^2}{r^2}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Charged Einstein-Rosen: coordinates $(t, u, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\dfrac{u^2}{u^2 + r_q^2}c^2dt^2 + du^2 + \left(u^2 + r_q^2\right)\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Einstein-Rosen Waves

Exact vacuum solutions describing gravitational waves with cylindrical wave fronts and a single polarisation, converging on an axis, passing through it and spreading out again. Einstein's equations for them reduce to the flat cylindrical wave equation for one function and a quadrature for a second.

- id: `einstein_rosen_waves`
- tags: vacuum, gravitational wave, cylindrical symmetry, exact solution, time-dependent, radiating, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/einstein_rosen_waves.json
- chart Cylindrical: coordinates $(t, \rho, \phi, z)$, $$ds^2 = e^{2(\gamma - \psi)}\left(-c^2dt^2 + d\rho^2\right) + \rho^2e^{-2\psi}d\phi^2 + e^{2\psi}dz^2$$
- chart Null: coordinates $(u, v, \phi, z)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{2(\gamma - \psi)}du\,dv + \dfrac{(v - u)^2}{4}e^{-2\psi}d\phi^2 + e^{2\psi}dz^2$$

### Elliptic de Sitter Space

De Sitter space with every event identified with the event opposite it on the hyperboloid, $X \sim -X$. One observer's horizon then bounds the whole world and future and past infinity are a single sphere. The spacetime has no closed timelike curves and no global direction of time.

- id: `elliptic_de_sitter`
- tags: de Sitter, positive cosmological constant, cosmological constant, maximally symmetric, constant curvature, not time orientable, topology, cosmological horizon, horizon, causal structure, holography, inflation, expanding universe, cosmology, homogeneous, isotropic, geodesically complete, no singularity, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model, Einstein space, conformally flat, stationary, static, spherically symmetric
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/elliptic_de_sitter.json
- chart Global: coordinates $(t, \chi, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + \ell^2\cosh^2(ct/\ell)\left(d\chi^2 + \sin^2\chi\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Conformal: coordinates $(\eta, \chi, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{\ell^2}{\cos^2\eta}\left(-d\eta^2 + d\chi^2 + \sin^2\chi\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Kruskal: coordinates $(U, V, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = \dfrac{\ell^2}{\left(1 - UV\right)^2}\left(-4\,dU\,dV + \left(1 + UV\right)^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Static: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{r^2}{\ell^2}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{1 - \dfrac{r^2}{\ell^2}} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Planar: coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + e^{2ct/\ell}\left(dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2\right)$$

### Ellis-Bronnikov Traversable Wormhole

A static, spherically symmetric traversable wormhole with zero redshift function, also known as the drainhole metric.

- id: `ellis_bronnikov`
- tags: wormhole, exotic matter, traversable, static, spherically symmetric, stationary, scalar field, phantom field, energy condition violation, asymptotically flat, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/ellis_bronnikov.json
- chart Spherical: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + dr^2 + (r^2 + \ell^2)\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\, d\phi^2\right)$$

### Erez-Rosen Quadrupole

Schwarzschild's metric with a mass quadrupole added, a static vacuum field of Weyl's class found by G. Erez and Nathan Rosen in 1959. For every quadrupole parameter $q \neq 0$ a naked curvature singularity stands where the horizon was, which Doroshkevich, Zel'dovich, and Novikov used in 1965 to argue that a collapsing star sheds its quadrupole.

- id: `erez_rosen`
- tags: vacuum, static, stationary, axisymmetric, Weyl class, harmonic function, mass, quadrupole, prolate spheroidal coordinates, curvature singularity, naked singularity, directional singularity, no-hair theorem, gravitational collapse, asymptotically flat, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/erez_rosen.json
- chart Prolate Spheroidal: coordinates $(t, x, y, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{2\psi}c^2dt^2 + m^2e^{-2\psi}\left(e^{2\gamma}\left(x^2 - y^2\right)\left(\dfrac{dx^2}{x^2 - 1} + \dfrac{dy^2}{1 - y^2}\right) + \left(x^2 - 1\right)\left(1 - y^2\right)d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Spherical: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{2\psi}c^2dt^2 + e^{-2\psi}\left(e^{2\gamma}\left(r^2 - 2mr + m^2\sin^2\theta\right)\left(\dfrac{dr^2}{r^2 - 2mr} + d\theta^2\right) + \left(r^2 - 2mr\right)\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Exponential Metric of Papapetrou and Yilmaz

A static, spherically symmetric metric whose components are exponentials of the Newtonian potential, with no horizon, offered in place of Schwarzschild's and later shown to be a traversable wormhole held open by a scalar field of negative energy.

- id: `exponential_metric`
- tags: wormhole, traversable, no horizon, exotic matter, scalar field, phantom field, energy condition violation, asymptotically flat, isotropic coordinates, alternative theories of gravity, Yilmaz, Papapetrou, Lambert W function, singular horizon, static, stationary, spherically symmetric, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/exponential_metric.json
- chart Isotropic: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{-2m/r}c^2dt^2 + e^{2m/r}\left(dr^2 + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Cartesian: coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{-2m/r}c^2dt^2 + e^{2m/r}\left(dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2\right)$$
- chart Areal (curvature coordinates): coordinates $(t, R, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{-2m/r}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dR^2}{\left(1 - \dfrac{m}{r}\right)^2} + R^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Harmonic: coordinates $(t, u, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{-2m\,u}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{e^{2m\,u}}{u^2}\left(\dfrac{du^2}{u^2} + d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Fisher-Janis-Newman-Winicour Scalar Field

The static, spherically symmetric spacetime of a mass that also carries a massless scalar field, found by I. Z. Fisher in 1948 and found again by Allen Janis, Ezra Newman, and Jeffrey Winicour in 1968. For any scalar charge, however small, the sphere where Schwarzschild's horizon would stand has zero area and infinite curvature, and no horizon hides it.

- id: `fisher_jnw`
- tags: static, stationary, spherically symmetric, scalar field, massless scalar field, minimally coupled scalar field, Einstein-scalar, scalar charge, mass, naked singularity, curvature singularity, timelike singularity, no horizon, no-hair theorem, black hole mimicker, photon sphere, gravitational lensing, cosmic censorship, Janis-Newman-Winicour, JNW, Fisher solution, Wyman solution, anti-Fisher, harmonic coordinates, isotropic coordinates, asymptotically flat, exact solution, Lorentzian, Einstein equations, four-dimensional, idealized model
- signature: (-,+,+,+)
- full data: https://damiansowinski.com/MFS/assets/data/metrics/fisher_jnw.json
- chart Spherical: coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -f^{\gamma}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{f^{\gamma}} + f^{1-\gamma}r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Janis-Newman-Winicour: coordinates $(t, R, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -f^{\gamma}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dR^2}{f^{\gamma}} + f^{1-\gamma}\left(R + \dfrac{b(1+\gamma)}{2}\right)^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$
- chart Isotropic: coordinates $(t, \rho, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -h^{2\gamma}c^2dt^2 + \left(1 + \dfrac{b}{4\rho}\right)^4h^{2(1-\gamma)}\left(d\rho^2 + \rho^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right)$$
- chart Harmonic: coordinates $(t, u, \theta, \phi)$, $$ds^2 = -e^{-2mu}c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{k^2e^{2mu}}{\sinh^2(ku)}\left(\dfrac{k^2du^2}{\sinh^2(ku)} + d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)$$

### Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker Expanding Universe

The Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker metric describing a homogeneous, isotropic expanding universe.

- id: `frw`
